forward.signal: Early warning of a big move
forward.what: Flags sessions likely to be large, in either direction.
forward.why: 3 settled calls. Below 20 this is noise: a short run of hits cannot be told apart from luck.

forward.what: Whether the forecast band contains the share of outcomes it should.
forward.why: no outcome has settled yet - there is no evidence either way

forward.what: Stocks closing outside the band the model gave them.
forward.why: no outcome has settled yet - there is no evidence either way

historical.finding: The top 5% of scores preceded a big move 36.4% of the time, against a 9.4% base rate - a 3.9x lift.
historical.caveat: A backtest on data the rule was built from. It is the reason to watch the signal, not evidence that it works live.

historical.finding: Only the very high (>1.20) band beat the baseline: 1.62% average over 21 sessions against 0.98%, up in 68.2% of cases against 61.8%.
historical.caveat: Every other PCR band did worse than the baseline, so the folk reading of PCR is mostly wrong on this data.

historical.finding: The prior S&P session correlates 0.263 with Nifty's next one, explaining 6.9% of it.
historical.caveat: Weak on an average day - the relationship only sharpens in the tails, which is where the sample is thinnest.

note: 3 signals are being scored forward, with 3 settled calls between them. 0 are readable yet. 3 more are backtested studies, which are kept separate because a backtest is not a track record.

cautions.not_proven: Nothing on this page is called proven below 100 settled calls. A short run of hits cannot be told apart from luck.
cautions.backtest_is_not_record: A backtest tests a rule on data its author could see. A track record tests it on data nobody had seen. Only the second is evidence, and the two are never added together.
cautions.misses_count: A hit rate is published with the misses it implies. A page showing only the winners is an advertisement.
cautions.no_advice: This is a record of measurement, not a recommendation.
